lesson_title: Plan a Market Stall in Sixty Seconds
hook_text: Two learners planned a popcorn stall on one page, and made more than they expected. Here is their plan.
clip_script: Step one: guess your sales. 120 bags at R10: R1 200 income. Step two: fixed costs. Table hire R100, sign R50. Step three: variable costs. R4 a bag for kernels, oil and bags: R480. Step four: subtract. R1 200 minus R630: R570 expected profit. Market day: they sell 150 bags. Favourable! But oil cost more, R5 a bag. Unfavourable. Real profit: R600. Lesson: make more popcorn, find cheaper oil. That is a business budget: plan, sell, compare, improve.
visual_style: A whiteboard market stall with a one-page budget beside it, numbers filling in, then green and red ticks for favourable and unfavourable.
mood: Energetic and hands-on, a mini entrepreneur challenge.
pacing: Four quick steps, a market-day reveal, then a fast compare.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and plan a one-page budget for a stall you would love to run.
